source_text: Alio die cum pranderemus, subito rapti sumus ut audiremur. Et peruenimus ad forum. Rumor statim per uicinas fori partes cucurrit, et factus est populus immensus. Ascendimus in catastam. Interrogati ceteri confessi sunt. Uentum est et ad me. Et apparuit pater ilico cum filio meo, et extraxit me de gradu dicens: Supplica; miserere infanti. Et Hilarianus procurator, qui tunc loco proconsulis Minuci Timiniani defuncti ius gladii acceperat: Parce, inquit, canis patris tui, parce infantiae pueri. Fac sacrum pro salute imperatorum. Et ego respondi: Non facio. Hilarianus: Christiana es? inquit. Et ego respondi: Christiana sum. Et cum staret pater ad me deiciendam, iussus est ab Hilariano proici, et uirga percussus est. Et doluit mihi casus patris mei, quasi ego fuissem percussa: sic dolui pro senecta eius misera. Tunc nos uniuersos pronuntiat et damnat ad bestias; et hilares descendimus ad carcerem. Tunc quia consueuerat a me infans mammas accipere et mecum in carcere manere, statim mitto ad patrem Pomponium diaconum, postulans infantem. Sed pater dare noluit. Et quomodo deus uoluit, neque ille amplius mammas desiderat, neque mihi feruorem fecerunt, ne sollicitudine infantis et dolore mammarum macerarer.
thought_title: Questioned before the procurator and condemned
orientation: Perpetua is speaking in her prison diary as the group is brought to the forum for interrogation.
pass_a_gloss: On another day when we were eating lunch, suddenly we were seized to be heard. And we arrived at the forum. A rumor immediately ran through the neighboring parts of the forum, and an immense crowd came to be. We went up onto the platform. The others when interrogated confessed Christ. It came also to me. And father appeared at once with my son, and he pulled me down from the step saying: Make the offering; pity the baby. And Hilarianus the procurator, who then in place of the dead proconsul Minucius Timinianus had received the power of the sword: Spare, he said, the gray hairs of your father, spare the infancy of the boy. Make a sacred act for the health of the emperors. And I answered: I do not do it. Hilarianus: Are you a Christian woman? he said. And I answered: I am a Christian woman. And when father stood by to cast me down, he was ordered by Hilarianus to be thrown out, and he was beaten with a rod. And the fall of my father pained me, as if I myself had been beaten: so I grieved for his wretched old age. Then he pronounces upon us all together and condemns us to the wild beasts; and cheerful we went down to prison. Then because the baby had been accustomed to receive the breasts from me and to remain with me in prison, at once I send to my father Pomponius the deacon, requesting the baby. But father refused to give him. And as God willed, neither does he desire the breasts further, nor did they make fever for me, lest I should be worn away by worry for the baby and by pain of the breasts.

pass_b_english: One day while we were eating lunch, we were suddenly seized for a hearing. We were brought to the forum. Rumor spread at once through the quarters around the forum, and an immense crowd formed. We went up onto the platform. When the others were questioned, they confessed Christ.

Then my turn also came. My father appeared at once with my son. He pulled me down from the step and said, "Make the offering. Have pity on the baby." Hilarianus the procurator, who had then received the power of the sword in place of the dead proconsul Minucius Timinianus, said, "Spare your father's gray hairs. Spare the child's infancy. Make a sacred act for the welfare of the emperors." I answered, "I will not do it." Hilarianus said, "Are you a Christian?" I answered, "I am a Christian."

While my father stood there to pull me down, Hilarianus ordered him to be thrown out. He was beaten with a rod. My father's fall grieved me as if I myself had been beaten. So I grieved for his wretched old age. Then he pronounced sentence on all of us and condemned us to the wild beasts. We went down to the prison cheerfully.

My baby had been used to nursing at my breast and staying with me in prison. So I sent Pomponius the deacon to my father at once to ask for the baby. But my father would not give him. As God willed it, the baby no longer wanted the breast. My breasts did not become inflamed, so that I would not be worn out by worry for the baby and pain in my breasts.
